preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10 000) representing the length of the ciphered text.
The second line of input is a string of exactly n lowercase English letters representing the ciphered text t.
The third line of input is an integer m (1 ≤ m ≤ 100 000) representing the number of words in the list.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(word) <= 1000 for word in stdin.splitlines()[3:])
preconditions.description: Each of the next m lines contains a non-empty word wi (|wi| ≤ 1 000) consisting of uppercase and lowercase English letters.
The total length of all words does not exceed 1 000 000.

postconditions.description: The output is a valid sentence composed of words from the given list, where each word is used in its original form (case preserved).

postconditions.expression: all(word in stdin.splitlines()[3:] for word in original_words)
postconditions.description: Each word in the output sentence must be present in the given list of words.
The concatenation of the reversed lowercase versions of the words in the output sentence must exactly match the ciphered text t.
